functionalObligations.text: The obligor is not the brand: the June 2026 examination states that USD1 is issued and redeemed by BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A., a national trust bank chartered and supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, while the USD1 brand and certain associated trademarks are owned and controlled by World Liberty Financial, Inc. and SC Financial Technologies, LLC.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a CORPUS CORRECTION that changes the instrument's category. The corpus treats World Liberty Financial as the issuer with 'reserves custodied at BitGo'. The attested position is that an OCC-supervised national trust bank issues and redeems, and WLF owns the brand. Every residue item beginning 'the issuer as obligor' must be re-pointed. Separately, the separation of brand-owner from obligor is itself a fact with no symbol: no element can say that the party whose name is on the token is not the party that owes you.

functionalObligations.text: The claim is contractual and confers no interest in any asset: 'USD1 holders' redemption rights are contractual and do not constitute a security interest in, or direct property interest in, any specific reserve asset.'
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the single most important sentence in the USD1 record. It is the answer to 'what happens if the issuer cannot pay', it is the OPPOSITE of Circle's bare-legal-title property assertion and the OPPOSITE of Paxos's segregated-trust priority claim, and all three are At in the model. Against that, the assets sit in segregated FBO accounts at an OCC-supervised trust bank, which makes the holder's position materially better than USDT's and materially worse than the property claim USDC asserts. Three positions on one axis, one symbol.

functionalObligations.text: Only registered customers of the issuer in Good Standing may mint or redeem; persons who hold USD1 without an account are 'Users' who may transfer USD1 on supported networks but do not have direct redemption rights with the Company.
functionalObligations.note: BOTH APPROXIMATE. Rd asserts a right the attestation expressly denies to non-account holders. Aw is a CORPUS DEPARTURE, added on the corpus's own USDC reasoning (Clients in Good Standing versus Users). CORPUS CORRECTION to the Rd marker: the corpus says 'institutional-only, contractual, discretionary'. Contractual and discretionary are right; 'institutional-only' is NOT stated -- the terms say registered customers in Good Standing, which is a KYC and sanctions test, not an institutional test. Law L16 is not satisfied: transfers are permissionless.

functionalObligations.text: No redemption minimum, fee schedule or settlement time is published: the governing terms describe only submission through the issuer's platform, compliance review, and settlement timing.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Minimum, fee and latency are UNKNOWN from the primary documents reachable in stage 1, and are not repaired from press or aggregators. The gap matters for the same reason it matters at USDT: the three parameters that decide whether the peg holds under stress are neither in the model nor, here, in the public record.

functionalObligations.text: The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$4,634,586,966 against 4,634,410,387 redeemable tokens outstanding -- a surplus of US$176,579 -- held as US$1,178,613,044 in demand deposit accounts and US$3,455,973,922 in a government money market fund at NAV under CUSIP 31607A703, with zero in the issuer's own bank account.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, with a qualification the corpus gets backwards. USD1's reserve is NARROWER than the corpus implies -- 'reserve portfolio (custodied at BitGo)' suggests a portfolio; it is bank deposits plus one government money market fund, with no directly held Treasuries, no repo, no gold and no loans. The vocabulary cannot express that USD1's reserve is nameable in one line where Tether's takes a table, and that difference is the difference between a boring instrument and an interesting one. CUSIP 31607A703 resolves to the Fidelity Investments Money Market Government Portfolio per third-party securities reference; the fund is NOT named in the attestation and this identification is not an issuer claim.

functionalObligations.text: Cash sits in demand-deposit and money-market-deposit accounts at US commercial banks regulated by the Federal Reserve, in segregated accounts titled to BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. for the benefit of USD1 stablecoin holders, with the attestation noting that balances at times may exceed the FDIC limit of US$250,000; no bank is named.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two unnameable facts in one sentence: which banks hold the cash (UNKNOWN), and that the deposit insurance which is the retail reader's mental model of 'a bank account' does not reach the balance. The FDIC-limit caveat is the issuer telling you, in the attestation, that the segregation is legal rather than insured -- and At has no slot for a caveat.

functionalObligations.text: Eligible reserve assets are contractually limited to cash, cash equivalents, short-term US Treasuries, fully Treasury-collateralised reverse repurchase agreements and government money market funds.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A rule that FORBIDS the issuer from holding certain assets is a constraint on the reserve, and the reserve has no representation, so the constraint has nothing to bind. This is the single largest design difference between USD1 and USDT -- an enforceable eligible-asset list against a discretionary portfolio containing gold, bitcoin, equities and secured loans -- and both decompose with At.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer is also the custodian: BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. issues, redeems and holds the reserve.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION to the corpus's framing. The corpus records custody as a distinct residue on the ground that no element distinguishes 'issuer holds reserves' from 'custodian holds reserves for issuer'. True -- and here the distinction COLLAPSES, because one entity is both, which is a third case the vocabulary also cannot record. Compare USDC, where manager (BlackRock) and custodian (BNY) are two further separate parties.

functionalObligations.text: Assurance is a monthly examination by KPMG LLP, San Francisco, of the issuer's management assertion, signed 2026-07-31, under AICPA attestation standards against the AICPA 2025 Criteria for Stablecoin Reporting: Specific to Asset-Backed Fiat-Pegged Tokens, Part I, at two report dates per month, with reports published back to April 2025.
functionalObligations.note: The best L27 fit of the five, and still incomplete: named attester yes, independence yes, stated assurance yes, and uniquely a NAMED PUBLIC CRITERIA SET against which the assertion is examined. Staleness bound: cadence by practice, not covenant. Recourse: none. At cannot record that this examination is against the AICPA 2025 stablecoin criteria while USDT's is an ISAE 3000R engagement on a bespoke schedule and USDG's is under Singapore ISCA standards -- three incomparable subject matters under one symbol.

functionalObligations.text: The seizure machinery is armed and, at the report date, unused: the June 2026 report records that with respect to USD1 there are no time-locked tokens, test tokens, or access-restricted tokens in the reporting period.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Fz is a capability predicate and cannot record exercise. 'The power exists and has never been used' and 'the power exists and 2,000 addresses are frozen' produce identical decompositions, and USD1 and USDT are respectively those two cases. This is the same defect as USDT F17's latent fee dial seen from the other side: the vocabulary cannot say armed-and-unused any more than it can say installed-but-dormant.

functionalObligations.text: A freezer may immobilise an address, and the freeze predicate is checked in _transfer and _approve against from, to AND msg.sender, so freezing an address also disables it as a spender of other people's allowances.
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note. RESIDUE WITHIN THE ASSIGNMENT: no symbol distinguishes freezing a BALANCE from freezing an ACTOR. Freezing a relayer or a market-maker contract here disables it for every counterparty who has approved it, which is a blast radius Fz cannot express.

functionalObligations.text: The owner may seize a frozen balance in full: drain(address) requires the account to be frozen and moves its entire balance to owner(), emitting FrozenAccountDrained.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. This is confiscation, not freezing. Fz names it identically to USDT's destroy (which annihilates rather than seizes) and to USDC's blacklist (which does neither). Three consequences for a holder -- immobilised, annihilated, transferred to the issuer -- one symbol.

functionalObligations.text: The owner may forcibly re-assign a frozen balance to a different address: reallocate(address _from, address _to, uint256 _amount) requires _from to be frozen and transfers to a replacement account, emitting FrozenFundsReallocated.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and the sharpest instance of Fz's collapse. The intended use is key-loss recovery -- re-issuing a holder's own position to a new address -- which is a FORCED TRANSFER WITH A BENIGN PURPOSE, and it is indistinguishable in the vocabulary from confiscation. USD1 holds all three powers (freeze, drain, reallocate); PYUSD holds two (freeze, wipe); USDT holds two (freeze, destroy); USDC holds one. Fz is present on all four.

functionalObligations.text: A pauser may halt all transfers: pause() and unpause() are present in the verified implementation and held by PAUSER_ROLE and UNPAUSER_ROLE in the governor; paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED. Verified in the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04 (pause, unpause both present) and separated into two roles in the governor, which is finer than any other member of the five. Adding Gp here and at USDT is what breaks the corpus's claimed identity USDT = USD1 against USDC's set.

functionalObligations.text: The token is an EIP-1967 transparent proxy at 0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B98A4FA4921476f08B0d with implementation StablecoinV2 at 0x694aA534BdeF8Ed63244eb902E7914e527891F08 (solc 0.8.24, fully verified 2026-04-05) and a separate ProxyAdmin at 0xa032Fe6C496732bdfc0d235066F55f171FA4aecE.
functionalObligations.note: Firm fit. There is no public source repository for StablecoinV2 or TokenGovernor and neither declares a license; the canonical artefact is the fully verified deployed source, matched by metadata hash. 'Deployed matches a repo' is not applicable -- there is no repo -- which is a third case beside 'matches' and 'does not match' that no element records.

functionalObligations.text: Upgrade authority and token authority are held by two different quorums with no delay on either: the ProxyAdmin's owner is a Gnosis Safe at 0x6a8dc6dbf909f542f2536edf8676d52630cf59e1 with 5 owners and threshold 3, while the token's owner is TokenGovernor at 0xEE9b1a09aEdaCED9dCDa74964EA447FEB93861c2 whose DEFAULT_ADMIN is a different Safe at 0x0d190b74308669e8f4fe7dbce3466169b285289d with 6 owners and threshold 3.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xee9b1a09aedaced9dcda74964ea447feb93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call of the EIP-1967 admin slot at 0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B98A4FA4921476f08B0d, owner() on the ProxyAdmin, and getThreshold()/getOwners() on both Safes (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Tg is correctly ABSENT -- neither Safe has a timelock -- so law L15 is NOT satisfied, exactly as at USDC and PYUSD. The separation of upgrade authority from token authority into two distinct 3-of-N quorums is a real and deliberate control-plane design and the carrier has no party sort in which to state it. Prohibition X9 does not fire on a 3-of-N, so the tables again treat a three-signature immediate upgrade as unremarkable.

functionalObligations.text: Token authority is decomposed into nine named roles in TokenGovernor -- MINTER_ROLE, BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE, BURNER_ROLE, FREEZER_ROLE, UNFREEZER_ROLE, PAUSER_ROLE, UNPAUSER_ROLE, RECOVERY_ROLE and CHECKER_ADMIN_ROLE -- with DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE reserved for drainFrozenAccount, batchDrainFrozenAccounts and executeTokenFunction; minters and burners are the admin Safe plus two further addresses, freezers the admin Safe plus one, pausers the admin Safe plus one.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xee9b1a09aedaced9dcda74964ea447feb93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getAdmins(), getMinters(), getBurners(), getFreezers(), getPausers(), getBridgeMintersOrBurners(), getChecker() at 0xEE9b1a09aEdaCED9dCDa74964EA447FEB93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. This is the finest-grained control plane of the five -- freeze and unfreeze are separate roles, pause and unpause are separate roles -- and the model records exactly Fz and Gp for it, the same two symbols it records for USDT's single 3-of-6 key. The vocabulary's resolution on the control plane is one bit per facility, and the category's real variation is entirely inside that bit.

functionalObligations.text: A compliance checker can be installed at any time and is not installed: TokenGovernor exposes setChecker() for an IChecker, and getChecker() reads the zero address at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, new -- not in the corpus. A transfer-time permission gate is ABSENT BUT ONE TRANSACTION AWAY. Aw is correctly not assigned for this (the gate does not exist today), and the vocabulary has no way to record that it is armed. The same shape recurs three times in this category: USDT's zero-valued but owner-settable transfer fee, this null-but-installable checker, and USDG's capabilities that exist only while an admin-controlled dispatch table maps their selectors. That is a category-level gap: THE VOCABULARY DESCRIBES WHAT IS, NOT WHAT IS ARMED.

functionalObligations.text: Ownership cannot be dropped: renounceOwnership() reverts.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE of the kind the options lane named: this is a guarantee discharged BY CONSTRUCTION -- the state 'no owner' cannot arise -- and the requirement language admits only discharge by naming a satisfying element. A deliberately permanent control plane and an unexamined one produce the same record.

functionalObligations.text: USD1 moves between chains by burning and minting under Chainlink CCIP, corroborated on-chain by a dedicated BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE held by two addresses, 0xf9e47d3720d5142930444ae6773c7f6d05696228 and 0x36a72ed0096b414521c45e3ddc9ed657d1d9c141, over native issuance on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Tron, Aptos and Tempo and eleven documented deployments.
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Xf and Xm are ADDED. The corpus says explicitly 'the token is deployed natively on multiple chains by the issuer, again not Xf'. That is now wrong on both the documentation and the chain: burn-and-mint over a message-verifying protocol is Xf plus Xm, and the code itself agrees -- a bridge mint/burn role would not exist if bridge-driven supply were not a distinct authority. This is genuine MECHANISM and it is the second refutation of the claim that every symbol these five use is control-plane or attestation.

functionalObligations.text: Bridge-driven supply is a different authority from treasury-driven supply: BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE is separate from MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE and is held by different addresses.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xee9b1a09aedaced9dcda74964ea447feb93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getMinters(), getBurners(), getBridgeMintersOrBurners() at 0xEE9b1a09aEdaCED9dCDa74964EA447FEB93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Xf does not distinguish supply created against an incoming cross-domain message from supply created against an incoming wire, and this deployment separates them explicitly in code because they are different risks. The corpus's cross-domain group names the movement and not the authority behind it.

functionalObligations.text: A holder may authorise transfers by signature: the implementation exposes EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization, cancelAuthorization and batchCancelAuthorization together with EIP-2612 permit.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT the corpus codes for none of the five. Law L17's four terms are satisfied exactly -- bounded scope (one amount, one payee), revocation (cancelAuthorization, and uniquely a batch form), expiry (validAfter/validBefore) and nonce plus EIP-712 domain separation. Approximate only against Au's 'session policy' gloss: this is single-shot delegation. Verified from the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04.

functionalObligations.text: The token has 18 decimals rather than the category's usual 6, and Ethereum supply is 1,529,515,526.739243049392059492 at 2026-08-04 against attested all-chain outstanding of 4,634,410,387 across six chains, of which BNB Smart Chain is the larger leg at 1,802,654,137.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: no element names a fixed-unit balance. RANKING BASIS NOTE: attested outstanding is 4,634,410,387 against the corpus's DefiLlama US$4.00B; the Ethereum leg alone is 1.53bn, so a single-chain reading understates by roughly three times. Decimals differ from every other member of the five and nothing in the model records the unit.
